blueprint_topic: Management of Care — interdisciplinary collaboration with respiratory therapy, regulated role boundaries, and authorized respiratory-care activities
stem: A nurse is reviewing roles before collaborating with a respiratory therapist (RT). Using the AARC Model Practice Act as a model rather than a substitute for state law, which RT activity is consistent with its description of respiratory care?

options.A: Administer prescribed respiratory-care agents, monitor the client's response to treatment and testing, and act or report within authorized orders or protocols.
options.B: Administer prescribed respiratory-care agents and independently expand the medication regimen when the response is inadequate, without additional order or protocol authority.
options.C: Perform respiratory diagnostic testing and equipment setup, while leaving assessment of the client's treatment response to nursing because RT scope excludes monitoring.
options.D: Initiate routine respiratory treatment from unit custom when no order or protocol exists, provided the intervention is within the therapist's training and competency.

rationale: A is correct. The current AARC webpage hosting its Model Practice Act states that the model outlines provisions common in licensure laws and is advocated as a model for state regulation. In the model definition of respiratory-care practice, AARC includes administration of pharmacologic, diagnostic, and therapeutic agents related to respiratory-care procedures prescribed by a physician; implementation of written or verbal orders; observation and monitoring of signs, symptoms, behavior, and physical responses to respiratory treatment and diagnostic testing; and reporting, referral, protocol-based action, or treatment changes pursuant to authorized orders. The model also allows initiation of emergency procedures under board regulations or other authority. B is incorrect because the model does not grant unrestricted authority to independently expand a medication regimen outside applicable orders or protocol authority. C is incorrect because monitoring the client's response to respiratory treatment and diagnostic testing is explicitly included in the model description. D is incorrect because routine treatment is not authorized merely by unit custom when no order or protocol authority exists; the model separately recognizes emergency procedures only when permitted by board regulation or the Act. Actual RT scope must still be determined by applicable state law, regulation, credentialing, and facility policy.
educational_objective: Recognize respiratory therapy as a direct-care interdisciplinary discipline whose model scope includes prescribed respiratory therapies and monitoring of treatment response, while verifying actual authority under applicable law and policy.

NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan Management of Care: identify and collaborate with multidisciplinary team members, verify/implement provider orders, follow legal/ethical requirements, and recognize professional role boundaries.
source_claim_supported: Current official AARC HTML directly supports the modeled RT activities and explicitly frames the text as model state legislation rather than universal state law. NCSBN supports the nursing collaboration, order-verification, and role-boundary construct.

pdf_visual_verification: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan Management of Care evidence was visually verified earlier in this cleanup session. AARC evidence used for Q1920 is current HTML; no AARC PDF evidence is used.
correction_summary: Original Q1920 had a uniquely longest correct answer (133 characters versus 88-101) and distractors that were easy to eliminate. The stem was rebuilt to make explicit that the AARC text is model legislation rather than universal state law. All four options were rewritten as realistic scope/authority distinctions with closely balanced lengths and without absolute-word cueing.

option_audit.A: Correct; directly tracks the AARC model's prescribed respiratory-agent administration, monitoring, and authorized reporting/protocol action.
option_audit.B: Plausible autonomy overreach; incorrect because the model does not authorize unrestricted medication-regimen expansion outside applicable orders/protocol authority.
option_audit.C: Plausible interdisciplinary-boundary misconception; incorrect because treatment-response monitoring is explicitly part of the AARC model description of respiratory care.
option_audit.D: Plausible competency-based shortcut; incorrect because training/competency alone does not create order/protocol authority for routine treatment; emergency authority is separately conditioned on regulation/law.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on only/all/always/never/must-type absolute wording.
cueing_audit.answer_length: Final option lengths: A 159, B 174, C 168, D 166 characters; the correct answer is not the longest and choices are tightly balanced.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four alternatives describe plausible RT clinical activities and differ primarily in authority/scope details rather than obvious tone or structure.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified in the pre-stage audit. B exceeds order/protocol authority, C contradicts explicit monitoring language, and D substitutes unit custom/competency for legal or ordered authority. Post-fetch adversarial reread remains required.
